answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with work-backed identity: every identity must keep completing small verifiable tasks, such as checking data or grading peers, to stay active, like a willow that only stays green while it keeps drawing water. A fake identity costs real compute to maintain, so spinning up thousands of them is expensive, and idle or copied identities wither away. At the zenith of trust sit identities with long unbroken work histories, while new ones start at umber-level standing and must earn their way up by doing useful work rather than buying reputation.
